full_text: (a) A person commits the offense of aggravated assault when he or she assaults: (1) With intent to murder, to rape, or to rob; (2) With a deadly weapon or with any object, device, or instrument which, when used offensively against a person, is likely to or actually does result in serious bodily injury; or (3) A person or persons without legal justification by discharging a firearm from within a motor vehicle toward a person or persons. (b) Except as provided in subsections (c) and (d) of this Code section, aggravated assault is a felony punishable by imprisonment for not less than one nor more than 20 years.

(a) A person commits the offense of simple assault when he or she either: (1) Attempts to commit a violent injury to the person of another; or (2) Commits an act which places another in reasonable apprehension of immediately receiving a violent injury. (b) Except as provided in subsections (c) and (d) of this Code section, a person convicted of the offense of simple assault shall be punished as for a misdemeanor.

(a) A person commits the offense of battery when he or she intentionally causes substantial physical harm or visible bodily harm to another. (b) A person commits the offense of battery when, in a public place and with criminal intent, he or she intentionally strikes another person or touches another person in a rude and insolent manner.

(a) A person commits the offense of theft by taking when he or she unlawfully takes or, being in lawful possession thereof, unlawfully appropriates any property of another with the intention of depriving him or her of the property, regardless of the manner in which the property is taken or appropriated.

(a) A contract is an agreement between two or more parties for the doing or not doing of some specified thing. (b) To constitute a valid contract, there must be parties able to contract, a consideration moving to the contract, the assent of the parties to the terms of the contract, and a subject matter upon which the contract can operate.

(a) Upon the filing of a petition for divorce, the court may grant a temporary order for alimony and child support. (b) The court shall consider the financial resources of both parties and the needs of the child when determining the amount of child support.
